answer: Reviewers stake before they read, and one review in ten is re-checked cold by a second reviewer. A pass that fails the re-check slashes the first reviewer, and that one rule is what keeps the queue honest. Each submission carries a fresh nonce, so a captured answer cannot be resubmitted from a second account. The trail stays crystal clear about who signed which verdict. An attacker pays the stake behind every wrong approval, and the wharf ledger records it per call rather than per account, with no timber to hide behind.
